items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: I played with Joe Baraka, Leon Rapolo, and Bill Gallaty.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. What other bands did you play with?
Well, I played with Joe Baraka, Leon Rapolo, and Bill Gallaty.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-21
items.q: Bill Gallaty was the leader, or the manager of the band. And he played valve trombone... and I played the clarinet. ... That is, I took odd jobs with him.

ctx.x: oh what estimates did they play I didn't get that oh you didn't get it well I'll tell you

Susu Ramis played guitar Willie guitar played bass Harry Nunez played violin and I played the comic we played in the downtown section that is way down below Elysian Fields Avenue now this is 19 2 3 and 4 and 5 no night I made ahead I went ahead of my statement 19 3 4 and 5 and maybe 6 the uptown band I played with a boy named George Gieffer George Gieffer bass Joe Taranto guitar Freddie Inglot this boy sells ice cream around the streets today violin and Nick LaRocca this group this group and all the above groups…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-21
items.q: And a fellow named by the name of Palaszczuk played clarinet... and I played the clarinet. I followed a boy in there by the name of a Dykeman... prior to me coming into his band.

ctx.x: came and appeared, Mrs. Alice, how do you pronounce her? Alice, Alice Kern. Alice Kern, K-I-E-R-N. A female person over the age of majority and full well known unto me notary public, who first being duly sworn, disposed and said as follows, that deponent was well acquainted with and has personally known for more than 25 years, one Dominic J. La Rocca, who resides in the city of New Orleans, state of Louisiana. A deponent is an organist by profession and during a period of time from 1914 to 1916, set down on paper…

Now, you wanted to ask me about the band that played in Bill Gallaty's band? This man could have been around my age, if he was living today, maybe a year too older than me. He may be the father of some of these Gallaty boys playing around today. That I don't know, because I have never met any of these boys. But they played in the downtown section. Bill Gallaty was the leader, or the manager of the band. And he played valve trombone. They had a boy by the name of Tots, I don't know his right name, played drums.…
